text:
Jess (Finance): Hey team — customer ACME Corp flagged that their invoice for Jan shows 4,120 GPU-hours billed but our metering shows 3,800. Can someone confirm whether license line items or egress/KMS are being added on top?
Sam (InfraOps): Looking into infra logs. Do we have the per-instance GPU-hour breakdown for that tenant? I can pull from Prometheus/usage-db.
Leo (CustEng): Customer says their internal metering matches our exported CSV until mid-month then diverges. They suspect burst scale events.
Tara (Billing): We currently add a "Managed License" surcharge only for on-prem bundles. For VPC/private we were supposed to pass through vendor license as separate line. Did ACME opt into license pass-through? @billing-bot can you check subscription flags?
billing-bot: Subscription ACME-2029 PROVISIONING: plan=Private-VPC, license_pass_through=true, reserved_commitment=null
Sam (InfraOps): If license_pass_through is true, that shouldn't affect GPU-hours though. Maybe an instance type mismatch — some GPUs (A100 80GB) count as 1.5x for billing vs raw hours? We have a conversion factor in billing-config.
Jess (Finance): Good point. Tara, do we multiply by vGPU equivalence anywhere? If so, the invoice would show adjusted GPU-hours.
Tara (Billing): We apply a multiplier for "license units" when vendor charges are per physical GPU, but we also have a separate hardware-hours export. I'll attach the invoice CSV in a sec.
Leo (CustEng): I pulled the CSV from customer portal: rows look like:
```
2029-01-12,instance-x,gtx-40,120 hours
2029-01-18,scale-up,ml-a100,200 hours
```
But the invoice shows the ml-a100 line as 300 hours (1.5x). Customer says they weren't told about the multiplier.
Sam (InfraOps): That 1.5x comes from our license_equivalency table: ml-a100 -> 1.5. It's applied only when license_pass_through=true to compute vendor license charges. It should not alter the reported infra GPU-hours column. If invoice shows 300 in the GPU-hours column that's a bug in the invoice renderer.
Tara (Billing): Agree — probably a templating issue where the license_units column was printed twice. Quick test: I ran the invoice renderer for ACME in staging with their usage and it yielded GPU_HOURS=3800, LICENSE_UNITS=4200. Production render might have mis-bound variables.
Jess (Finance): Critical: customer is disputing the extra ~320 hours. Let's prepare a corrected invoice and a note explaining license vs infra lines. Action: Sam to confirm infra raw-hours, Tara to re-render invoice and remove license multiplier from GPU-hours cell, Leo to provide customer's portal extract, Jess to notify customer once fixed.
Sam (InfraOps): Running query now: promql -> sum by (tenant, gpu_type) (increase(gpu_instance_hours_total{tenant="acme"}[30d]))
I can share raw numbers in 20m.
Tara (Billing): I'll queue a hotfix to the invoice template. Ping me if you see similar tenant flags. ETA 3 hours.
Leo (CustEng): CC'ing the customer PM — informal update: we're investigating, expect corrected invoice within the day.
Jess (Finance): Thanks. Follow-ups: 1) Tara to add a test case for license_pass_through rendering; 2) Sam to add a reconciliation job that joins usage-db and billing export and alerts when delta > 5%; 3) Bill team to discuss whether reserved commitments should be invoiced separately vs amortized. Putting owner tags: Tara, Sam, Jess.
Tara (Billing): Noted. Also flagging that KMS/HSM and NAT egress are separate pass-throughs — confirm these are separate line items so customers don't conflate them with GPU-hours.
billing-bot: Ticket created: BILL-ACME-1918, priority=high, owners=[Tara,Sam], due=1918463989
Jess (Finance): Good. We'll update ACME after fix. :thumbsup:
